24	// Transcripts are append-only JSONL, but every checkpoint used to re-redact them
25	// from byte zero: a 70MB Codex rollout cost ~67s per Stop hook, and a session
26	// with N checkpoints re-redacted O(N^2) bytes overall. Redaction is ~99.7% of
27	// that write path (git object writing is milliseconds), and it is by far the
28	// dominant cost of a Stop hook on a large session.
29	//
30	// So keep the redacted output for the prefix already processed and redact only
31	// what was appended. Correctness rests on two properties:
32	//
33	//   - Redaction is per-line and stateless (see redact.redactJSONLLines), so
34	//     redacting a prefix and a suffix separately and concatenating them yields
35	//     exactly what redacting the whole file would. redact's own tests pin this
36	//     as redact(A+B) == redact(A)+redact(B) for newline-terminated A.
37	//   - A cached prefix always ends immediately after a "\n". Because of that the
38	//     redacted prefix also ends with "\n", and plain byte concatenation
39	//     reproduces the full result with no boundary fixups.
40	//
41	// The prefix is only reused when the source bytes it covered still hash the
42	// same and the redaction rules have not changed. Anything else -- a rewritten
43	// transcript, a compaction, changed custom rules, a CLI upgrade -- falls back to
44	// redacting everything.
45	//
46	// Scope: this covers the shadow-branch metadata write only. Condensation
47	// (strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go) and the Stop finalize rewrite
48	// (strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go) still redact whole transcripts; they inherit
49	// the sharding in redact.JSONLContent but not the prefix reuse. Single-JSON-value
50	// transcripts (OpenCode export) get neither, since they have no line structure to
51	// split on.
52	
53	const (
54		// redactCacheDirName sits in the git common dir, NOT under .entire/, because
55		// anything inside the worktree metadata directory would be walked into the
56		// checkpoint tree and committed.
57		redactCacheDirName = "entire-redact-cache"
58	
59		// redactCacheMinBytes is the file size below which incremental reuse is not
60		// worth its bookkeeping; a small file redacts in milliseconds.
61		redactCacheMinBytes = 1 << 20 // 1MiB
62	)
63	
64	// redactPrefixEntry is the persisted record of one file's already-redacted
65	// prefix. Written atomically; a missing, unreadable, or stale entry simply means
66	// a full redaction.
67	type redactPrefixEntry struct {
68		// Fingerprint identifies the redaction rules that produced RedactedBlob.
69		Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint"`
70		// SourceBytes is the length of the source prefix covered, always ending
71		// immediately after a newline.
72		SourceBytes int `json:"source_bytes"`
73		// SourceHash is the SHA-256 of source[:SourceBytes], proving the prefix has
74		// not been rewritten underneath us.
75		SourceHash string `json:"source_hash"`
76		// RedactedBlob is the git blob holding the redacted prefix.
77		RedactedBlob string `json:"redacted_blob"`
78	}
79	
80	// redactCache reads and writes redactPrefixEntry records under a directory in
81	// the git common dir. A nil *redactCache disables incremental reuse, which is
82	// what every caller that cannot resolve the git dir gets.
83	type redactCache struct {
84		dir string
85	}

87	// newRedactCache returns a cache rooted at gitCommonDir, or nil when the
88	// directory is empty or cannot be created. Callers treat nil as "no caching".
89	func newRedactCache(gitCommonDir string) *redactCache {
90		if gitCommonDir == "" {
91			return nil
92		}
93		dir := filepath.Join(gitCommonDir, redactCacheDirName)
94		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
95			return nil
96		}
97		return &redactCache{dir: dir}
98	}
99	
100	// repoRedactCache resolves the prefix cache for repo, or nil when the git common
101	// directory is unavailable (a bare repository, for instance). Nil disables
102	// incremental reuse without failing the write.
103	//
104	// resolveGitCommonDir memoizes per worktree and the sibling shadow-branch and
105	// push-queue writes already warm it, so this is cheap to call per checkpoint.
106	func repoRedactCache(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) *redactCache {
107		dir, err := resolveGitCommonDir(ctx, repo)
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil
110		}
111		return newRedactCache(dir)
112	}
113	
114	// redactionFingerprint combines the redaction config with the CLI build. The
115	// build is a deliberately conservative proxy for the vendored betterleaks
116	// ruleset and the pipeline itself, neither of which is introspectable: an
117	// upgrade invalidates every cached prefix and costs one full redaction.
118	func redactionFingerprint() string {
119		return versioninfo.Version + ":" + versioninfo.Commit + ":" + redact.ConfigFingerprint()
120	}
121	
122	func (c *redactCache) path(treePath string) string {
123		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(treePath))
124		return filepath.Join(c.dir, hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])+".json")
125	}
126	
127	func (c *redactCache) load(treePath string) *redactPrefixEntry {
128		data, err := os.ReadFile(c.path(treePath))
129		if err != nil {
130			return nil
131		}
132		var entry redactPrefixEntry
133		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &entry); err != nil {
134			return nil
135		}
136		if entry.SourceBytes <= 0 || entry.SourceHash == "" || entry.RedactedBlob == "" {
137			return nil
138		}
139		return &entry
140	}

142	// storePrefix records the prefix just written so the next checkpoint can reuse
143	// it. sourceHash must be the digest of the whole of the source content, and blob
144	// the object holding its redacted form.
145	//
146	// Failures are silent: losing a cache entry only costs a full redaction next
147	// time.
148	func (c *redactCache) storePrefix(ctx context.Context, treePath, sourceHash string, sourceBytes int, blob plumbing.Hash) {
149		if c == nil {
150			return
151		}
152		data, err := json.Marshal(redactPrefixEntry{
153			Fingerprint:  redactionFingerprint(),
154			SourceBytes:  sourceBytes,
155			SourceHash:   sourceHash,
156			RedactedBlob: blob.String(),
157		})
158		if err != nil {
159			return
160		}
161		if err := jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic(c.path(treePath), data, 0o600); err != nil {
162			logging.Debug(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "redaction"),
163				"failed to store redaction prefix cache", slog.String("error", err.Error()))

165	}

169		// Redacted is the content to store. Nil means the caller must redact the
170		// whole content itself.
171		Redacted []byte
172		// SourceHash is the digest of the whole source, computed as a side effect of

174		SourceHash string
175		// StorePrefix reports whether the caller should record this result for the

180	// incrementalRedactionCandidate reports whether a stored file is worth prefix
181	// caching: a large, append-only, line-delimited session transcript.
182	//
183	// Both checks below are load-bearing for different reasons, so neither is
184	// redundant:
185	//
186	//   - The filename establishes append-only. Only full.jsonl is appended to;
187	//     transcript.jsonl (the compact transcript) is regenerated in full each
188	//     checkpoint and agent.ChunkFileName yields "full.jsonl.001" for oversized

190	//   - redact.IsLineDelimited establishes that splicing is sound. The filename
191	//     alone is not a safe proxy: OpenCode writes a single JSON object

193	//     of a single JSON value drops out of the field-aware pass into raw entropy
194	//     detection over partial JSON.

203	func redactIncrementally(
204		ctx context.Context,
205		repo *git.Repository,
206		cache *redactCache,
207		content []byte,
208		treePath string,
209	) redactResult {
210		if cache == nil || !incrementalRedactionCandidate(content, treePath) {
211			return redactResult{}
212		}
213	
214		// Only a file ending on a line boundary can be cached, because the reuse
215		// contract requires the stored prefix to end just after a "\n".
216		if content[len(content)-1] != '\n' {
217			return redactResult{}
218		}
219	
220		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "redaction")
221	
222		entry := cache.load(treePath)
223		if entry == nil || entry.Fingerprint != redactionFingerprint() || entry.SourceBytes > len(content) {
224			return redactResult{SourceHash: hashBytes(content), StorePrefix: true}
225		}
226	
227		// Hash the prefix and the remainder in one pass: Sum snapshots the digest
228		// without resetting it, so validating the prefix also yields the whole-content
229		// hash the caller stores, instead of a second pass over ~70MB.
230		digest := sha256.New()
231		digest.Write(content[:entry.SourceBytes])
232		prefixHash := hex.EncodeToString(digest.Sum(nil))
233		digest.Write(content[entry.SourceBytes:])
234		fullHash := hex.EncodeToString(digest.Sum(nil))
235	
236		// The prefix must still be byte-identical; a rewritten or compacted
237		// transcript invalidates it.
238		if prefixHash != entry.SourceHash {
239			logging.Debug(logCtx, "redaction prefix changed, redacting in full",
240				slog.String("path", treePath), slog.Int("prefix_bytes", entry.SourceBytes))
241			return redactResult{SourceHash: fullHash, StorePrefix: true}
242		}
243	
244		prefix, err := readBlobBytes(repo, plumbing.NewHash(entry.RedactedBlob))
245		if err != nil {
246			logging.Debug(logCtx, "cached redacted prefix unreadable, redacting in full",
247				slog.String("path", treePath), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
248			return redactResult{SourceHash: fullHash, StorePrefix: true}
249		}
250		// A prefix that does not end on a newline would corrupt the join, so refuse
251		// it rather than emit spliced output.
252		if len(prefix) > 0 && prefix[len(prefix)-1] != '\n' {
253			logging.Debug(logCtx, "cached redacted prefix does not end at a line boundary, redacting in full",
254				slog.String("path", treePath))
255			return redactResult{SourceHash: fullHash, StorePrefix: true}
256		}
257	
258		if entry.SourceBytes == len(content) {
259			// Nothing appended since the last checkpoint: the stored entry already
260			// describes exactly this content, so there is nothing to re-record.
261			return redactResult{Redacted: prefix}
262		}
263	
264		suffix := content[entry.SourceBytes:]

267		out = append(out, prefix...)

272			slog.Int("reused_bytes", entry.SourceBytes),

274	
275		return redactResult{Redacted: out, SourceHash: fullHash, StorePrefix: true}
276	}

278	func hashBytes(b []byte) string {
279		sum := sha256.Sum256(b)
280		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
281	}
282	
283	// readBlobBytes loads a blob's full contents.
284	func readBlobBytes(repo *git.Repository, hash plumbing.Hash) ([]byte, error) {
285		blob, err := repo.BlobObject(hash)
286		if err != nil {
287			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read blob %s: %w", hash, err)
288		}
289		reader, err := blob.Reader()
290		if err != nil {
291			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open blob %s: %w", hash, err)
292		}
293		defer func() { _ = reader.Close() }()
294	
295		// blob.Size is known, so read into an exact buffer: io.ReadAll grows by
296		// doubling and allocates roughly 2.3x the payload for a large transcript.
297		out := make([]byte, blob.Size)
298		if _, err := io.ReadFull(reader, out); err != nil {
299			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read blob %s: %w", hash, err)
300		}
301		return out, nil
302	}

@@ -673,6 +673,9 @@ The manual-commit strategy (`manual_commit*.go`) does not modify the active bran
 - **Supports multiple concurrent sessions** - checkpoints from different sessions in the same directory interleave on the same shadow branch
 - Condenses session logs to permanent `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on user commits
 - Every path that builds a stored transcript sanitizes before redacting; the committed paths also externalize images in between, giving **sanitize → externalize images → redact**. Sanitization is the agent's optional `agent.TranscriptSanitizer` capability, applied via `agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage`; it strips non-portable agent state (Codex's encrypted reasoning payloads and compaction blobs, which are bound to the originating session and cannot be replayed out of a checkpoint). The three paths are the Stop/shadow write (`lifecycle.go` sanitizes before `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` is written, then the metadata-dir walker redacts it into the shadow tree — **no externalization**, so inline images in a shadow transcript are subject to redaction and assets exist only under committed checkpoints), post-commit condensation (`prepareTranscriptForStorage` in `manual_commit_condensation.go`), and the Stop finalize full-session rewrite (`manual_commit_hooks.go`). Where all three steps run, order is load-bearing at each step: sanitizing first avoids externalizing images out of items about to be discarded (storing an asset whose referencing line disappears) and avoids redacting megabytes of ciphertext only to discard it — base64 is the pathological input for the entropy layer, so a large Codex rollout otherwise costs tens of seconds per Stop *and* per commit; externalizing before redaction is required because redaction would otherwise flag and destroy the high-entropy base64. Sanitization is idempotent, so downstream paths call it without knowing whether an upstream path already did (`checkpoint.sanitizeForAgentType` is the store's belt-and-braces call). The agent's own transcript is never modified. Coupling to respect: `SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize` is a growth baseline compared against the shadow transcript blob size in `sessionHasNewContent`, so it must be measured in the same sanitized (pre-externalization) coordinate — that is `CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline`; using the raw size makes the comparison false forever and the session silently stops condensing.
+- **Redaction cost and the two mechanisms that contain it.** Redaction dominates the Stop hook on a large session: it is ~99.7% of the metadata-walk blob write (git object writing is milliseconds), and ~82% of that is the betterleaks regex ruleset. Two things keep it bounded, and both rest on redaction being **per-line and stateless** (`redact.redactJSONLLines`) — a rule that looked at neighbouring lines would silently break both:
+  - `jsonlContentImpl` shards the line pass into ~1MiB byte-balanced groups across goroutines. Output is byte-identical to the sequential pass. Sharding is gated on an explicit `concurrencySafe` argument describing the **redactor**, not on which entry point was called: `String` is pure and opts in (including `batch.go`'s OPF-disabled fast path), while the OPF collector closures accumulate into a shared map/slice and pass `concurrencyUnsafeRedactor`.
